title: runtime: GPU SKU normalization + capability detection for selector v2
author: Yuki Sato
description: Motivation: Kernel auto-selection v2 needs stable, low-cardinality GPU identification + a consistent capability view (SM version, bf16/fp8 support, etc.). Today we rely on raw device names from NVML/CUDA which vary across drivers and environments (e.g., "NVIDIA A10", "NVIDIA A10G", cloud-specific suffixes, MIG labels). This causes (1) selector ambiguity, (2) telemetry cardinality blow-ups, and (3) hard-to-reproduce perf diffs across SKUs that should be treated the same. Summary of changes: Introduce a small normalization layer that maps multiple raw identifiers to a canonical GpuSku enum (L4, A10, A100_40GB, A100_80GB, H100_SXM, H100_PCIe, T4, V100; with an Unknown fallback). Add a GpuCapabilities struct derived from a mix of (a) CUDA device properties (major/minor SM), (b) NVML memory size (used only for known SKUs to disambiguate A100 40 vs 80 where possible), and (c) runtime heuristics for features relevant to kernel selection (supports_bf16, supports_fp8, supports_flash_attention_v2, preferred_matmul_accum). Wire this into the selector context (but keep selection behavior unchanged in this PR; follow-up PRs will read the normalized sku/caps). Also add unit tests using captured nvidia-smi/NVML name strings seen in prod + benchmark lab, including MIG/partitioned naming patterns. Design notes: Normalization is intentionally conservative. If we cannot confidently map a raw name to a known sku, we return Unknown and set a minimal capability set. Selector v2 will treat Unknown as "safe kernels only" in the table-driven registry. We also explicitly bucket GPU names for metrics: emit gpu_sku=<canonical> and gpu_sm=<major>.<minor> rather than the raw device name. This aligns with the telemetry cardinality review guidance (Thomas/Allison). Behavior: - Canonical SKU string format: nvidia_<family>_<variant> (e.g., nvidia_l4, nvidia_a10, nvidia_a100_80gb_sxm4, nvidia_h100_sxm). - MIG handling: If NVML reports a MIG device name, we parse the parent GPU name when present; otherwise treat as Unknown but still report sm version. - Cloud quirks: Normalize known aliases ("A10G" -> A10; "H100 PCIe" variants). - Determinism: normalization has a strict precedence order: explicit alias table -> regex family match -> memory disambiguation (only if it matches expected bounds) -> Unknown. Testing: Added table-driven unit tests for name parsing + capability derivation; added a small integration-style test that stubs the GPU info provider and asserts the selector context contains canonical sku + sm fields. Related: ENG-3925. Context: This is a dependency for kernel selector v2 and for making selection decision telemetry stable across regions and GPU fleet transitions.
commits: runtime/gpu: add GpuSku enum + canonical string formatting
runtime/gpu: implement NVML/CUDA name normalization and alias table
runtime/gpu: derive capabilities (sm, bf16/fp8, flash attention flags)
runtime/selector: plumb normalized sku + caps into SelectionContext
tests: add golden cases for A10/A100/H100/L4 + MIG naming variants
telemetry: swap raw device name label for canonical gpu_sku + gpu_sm
review_conversation: Grace Kim: Can we guarantee that A100 40 vs 80 disambiguation won't misclassify if NVML reports a slightly different total memory? We had issues on some drivers with a few hundred MB delta.

Yuki Sato (author): Good call. I tightened the bounds and made memory-based disambiguation opt-in only after a strong family match (A100). If it falls outside bounds, we now return nvidia_a100_unknown_mem and mark supports_fp8=false (safe default). Added tests for off-by-delta cases.
Noah Patel: Please document precedence and ensure selection is deterministic across restarts. Also, can we avoid regex allocations on the hot path?

Yuki Sato (author): Added a comment block in gpu_sku.cc describing precedence + determinism. Also switched regex to a small set of precompiled patterns + simple substring checks for the common cases (L4/A10/A100/H100).

Thomas Baird: Telemetry change looks right, but make sure we don't accidentally emit both raw and canonical labels during the transition. Also sample Unknown cases to avoid cardinality from raw names in logs.

Yuki Sato (author): Updated runtime_metrics to only emit gpu_sku + gpu_sm. Raw name is now debug-only in a sampled log line behind RUNTIME_GPU_DEBUG=1. Unknown is a single canonical value (nvidia_unknown).
Allison Grant: Any downstream dashboards expecting the old label? If this changes metric names/labels, we should call it out.
Yuki Sato (author): Kept metric name stable; only replaced the label value source. Added a short note in the internal metrics comment and pinged Aisha to update dashboard queries in the rollout PR.
Omar El-Sayed: Please add one test for MIG naming like "MIG 1g.10gb" to ensure we don't crash on split names.
Yuki Sato (author): Added gpu_sku_normalization_test cases for MIG with and without parent GPU info; both map to Unknown but preserve sm capability.
Grace Kim: LGTM after the memory-bound tightening. This should unblock the table-driven registry work.
